adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of death in elderly patients with stage II colon cancer and a significant reduction in recurrence and death in elderly patients who had stage III colon cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adjuvant chemotherapy in elderly stage II/III colon cancer patients is beneficial in terms of overall survival and disease-free survival.
the benefit of adjuvant treatment in elderly patients is less clear and that the decision to offer adjuvant chemotherapy should be individualised.

adjuvant chemotherapy is beneficial for elderly colon cancer patients with stage III and high-risk stage II disease, and the benefit of adjuvant therapy for patients with stage II disease is less certain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adjuvant chemotherapy has a positive effect on the overall survival in elderly patients with stage II and III disease.
adjuvant chemotherapy in elderly colon cancer was not beneficial for overall survival.
the adjuvant effect of chemotherapy in elderly colon cancer is not inferior to that in younger patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can estimate the adjuvant treatment effect in the elderly population using observational data.
adjuvant chemotherapy is not beneficial in patients aged 70 and older with stage II and III colorectal cancer.
adjuvant chemotherapy is beneficial for elderly colon cancer patients with a life expectancy of 10 years or more.
